answer: One concrete defense is a stake that grows with verified work. An agent must forge a reputation by completing paid tasks over time, and each successful job adds weight to its record. New identities start on a narrow ledge: they can take only small, cheap jobs, so flooding the ocean of the market with fresh sybils costs real effort and time before any of them earns trust. An attacker would have to pay that slow cost thousands of times, while honest agents keep compounding a history that is expensive to fake and cheap for peers to check.
